summary: Assistive audit and safe demote for adaptive inference profiles
description: Issue summary: Customer reports increased token latency and intermittent 502 errors after enabling an adaptive inference profile that changes batching, prefix caching, and applies q4 quantization heuristics. Request: assistive audit of the active profile, safe demote plan to revert aggressions without a full snapshot rollback, and list of diagnostics we can collect without service disruption. Impact: LuminaAI is observing ~3x 95th percentile latency for synchronous generate calls and occasional streaming disconnects for long-context chat sessions. This affects multiple customer routes pinned to Dedicated pool D-42. Customer is sensitive to traffic disruption and requests a staged, low-risk rollback path.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer enabled profile 'adaptive-high-eff' via console with settings: dynamic_batching=enabled, prefix_kv_cache=aggressive, quant_profile=q4_0_auto.
2) Send representative chat request (approx 1k tokens context + 250 token reply) to route 'lumina/qa' pinned to D-42.
3) Observe response latency spikes and intermittent 'stream disconnect' errors after 30-90s.
4) Some requests return 502 with 'worker OOM' in serving logs.
(Observed reproducible on ~2% of requests but spikes correlate with higher concurrent sessions.)
logs:
Representative log excerpts:
[2026-03-12T15:22:10Z] worker-17 ERROR serve: kernel launch failed: cuMemAlloc failed
[2026-03-12T15:22:11Z] router WARN route-selection: fallback to redwood-7b-q4_0 causing desync
[2026-03-12T15:22:12Z] stream-conn INFO disconnect: client closed during kv-load
Full trace links: https://logs.redwood.internal/lumina/D-42/2026-03-12-15 (customer-approved access shared)
investigation: Initial hypothesis: aggressive prefix_kv_cache combined with auto quantization is causing memory pressure on a subset of GPU variants; dynamic batching increases peak memory usage leading to OOMs and kernel failures. Evidence collected: recent heap/pagemap deltas show 20% higher reserved GPU memory when q4_0_auto is combined with aggressive KV prefetch. Observed mismatch: some nodes still running older kernel builds (svc-runtime v3.9.1) while optimizer agent pushed profile expecting v3.10. Partial finding: router fallbacks to a quantized variant trigger synchronous cold-load of caches which spikes allocation and occasionally fails. Correlation with increased concurrency confirmed via sampling (95th percentile concurrency up 1.8x since toggle).
customer_notes: Customer timeline: toggled adaptive profile at 2026-03-12T14:58Z after QA passed on staging. They need minimal downtime; prefer staged demote (traffic-split to safe variant) rather than full pool restart. Customer provided shadow traffic token set and agreed to additional telemetry collection for 1 hour.
next_steps:
1) Provide a low-risk plan: a) Create safe demote profile that disables aggressive prefix_kv_cache and sets quant_profile=q4_0_fixed (no auto). b) Route 5% of traffic to safe profile via traffic-split for 30 minutes; monitor 95p latency and 5xx rate. c) If stable, increase to 25% then 100% over 90 minutes. d) If OOMs persist, apply emergency throttle (max concurrent per-session) and snapshot the serving state for rollback.
2) Collect additional diagnostics: GPU memory delta per-request, kernel version mapping per-worker, and KV cache hit/miss histogram.
3) Prepare rollback artifacts: per-tenant snapshot id, pre-toggle metrics baseline, and a pre-built playbook for on-call SRE to run drain-and-demote commands.
playbook_commands: rwi admin snapshot create --pool D-42 --tag pre-demote-SUP-100779
rwi admin traffic-split set --route lumina/qa --profile safe-demote-v1 --percent 5

resolution: In Progress - safe-demote canary showing positive results. Planned rollout to 25% then full over next 90 minutes. Rollback plan: revert traffic-split to 100% original profile, run 'rwi admin snapshot restore --id <pre-demote-SUP-100779>' and drain affected workers. If kernel OOMs persist after revert, escalate to infra to reimage nodes and pin to svc-runtime v3.10.

Add a guarded 'memory-pressure' circuit-breaker that disables aggressive KV prefetch under high-reserved-memory
Document safe-demote playbook in Confluence and link in rollout UI
